section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1985

Category (B) claimed 97·2 per cent of the total accidental deaths registered during 1985 as against 96·8 per cent registered during 1984. Under this category the highest number of accidental deaths in 1985 was recorded under the head 'Accidental deaths on roads' (29,831) followed by 'Drowning' (21,592), 'By fire' (16,667), 'In railways' (13,307), 'By poisoning' (8,560), 'By snake biting' (3,940), 'By accidental fall from height' (2,321), 'By fire arms' (1,860), 'By accidental electrocution by appliances' (1,834) and 'By house collapse' (1,341). The remaining heads recorded the number of accidental deaths below 1,000. The remaining unimportant causes categorised as 'Other causes' recorded a total number of (30,980) accidental death cases during 1935 as against 29,659 cases in 1984 sharing 22·2 per cent of the total accidental deaths. During 1985 'Accidental deaths on roads' accounted for 21·3 per cent of the total accidental deaths in India followed by 'Drowning' (15.5%), 'By fire' (11.9%) and 'In railways' (9·5%).
